status: Planning now has a bounded native demand/supply/capacity workspace read for one Company/branch, an owner-local HTTP router and a strict Next transport/SSR cutover for the Planning scenario, recommendation, resource and calendar lists. The Planning owner remains pending/partial: shared composition mounting, a dedicated Rust package, planning calculate/cancel/release commands, CAS/idempotency receipts, audit/outbox writes, same-transaction Manufacturing/Inventory/Finance/Projects guards and browser acceptance remain open.

scope.workflowBoundary: The qualified slice reads the current Company/branch planning scenarios with their stored shortage arrays and comparison/capacity context, their one-to-one recommendations, the production resource register, resource-calendar overrides and unreleased planning allocations. It does not calculate a scenario, reserve or release capacity, approve/reject a recommendation, cancel a scenario, create a manufacturing order, post Finance, consume Inventory, write Projects facts or close any of the five workflows.
scope.domain: Planning actor policy (`records.read`, exact Planning module, selected-context expiry), exact Company identity, optional branch scope, bounded scenario/recommendation/resource/calendar/allocation counts, exact date/status/version/timestamp shapes, positive quantities and resource versions, bounded weekday arrays, one-to-one scenario/recommendation and resource/calendar coherence, exact shortage arithmetic, exact typed context (demand source, incoming supply, stock witnesses, allocations, operations, comparison) and independent approval state for approved recommendations and owner-cancellation review state for rejected recommendations.
scope.application: One `planning_workspace` use case requires the current actor before any repository call, reads only the actor Company/branch planning-owned sources and validates every bounded row before presentation.
scope.adapters: Read-only SQL over planning_scenarios, planning_recommendations, production_resources, production_resource_calendar and planning_resource_allocations. The caller's serializable Holding transaction is required. No Manufacturing specification/order, Commerce product, Inventory stock, Finance journal, Projects, Records, IAM or Workflow business row is read or written. No owner write is performed.
scope.http: Owner-local GET /api/v1/holdings/{holding_slug}/planning/workspace. Exact Host/Holding targets, exact HTTPS origin validation, duplicate/unknown query rejection, private/no-store plus no-referrer/nosniff responses, exact data envelope validation and bounded BusinessError status mapping. The composition backend receives transport facts only and must supply the normal Account session, current Company/branch/department scope, purchase admission and serializable owner read.
scope.transport: ERPX_NATIVE_PLANNING_CONFIG is strictly validated: loopback-only private base, reserved ports 3000/3001/3100/3101/3103/8080 plus 5432/5433/5435 and 3200-3299 excluded, exact HTTPS Holding origins, unique hosts/slugs, 250..30000 ms timeout, bounded cookie/context/workspace headers, exact scenario/recommendation/resource/calendar/allocation/context shapes, unique IDs and references, shortage arithmetic, Company/branch scope and a 2 MiB response bound. A configured failure never falls back to the retained reader.
scope.ssr: The Planning presenter uses the native workspace when ERPX_NATIVE_PLANNING_CONFIG is present. Native scenario rows replace the console plan options/cards, native recommendations replace the independent-review list, and native resources/calendar replace the resource configuration/capacity lists. A native register section renders shortages and unreleased capacity allocations. The retained specification, warehouse, product and demand-source labels are still loaded by the retained Planning workspace read and are used only as display labels. An unset configuration retains the legacy lists; once configured, an invalid or failed native read is surfaced rather than silently replaced.
scope.purchaseAndIdentity: The Next owned wrapper keeps the retained Planning module, `records.read` and `requireManufacturingPurchasedRead` (module `planning`, capability `planning.basic`) preflight ahead of the native read. This is a preflight, not an atomic owner unit; the composition backend must repeat current authority and purchase admission on its own serializable owner transaction.
scope.notClaimed: No planning scenario calculation, scenario cancellation, recommendation approval/rejection, capacity reservation/release, manufacturing-order release, resource/calendar command, CAS write, idempotency receipt, audit/outbox effect, same-transaction cross-owner guard, shared composition mount, dedicated root workspace package, browser journey, staging or production acceptance.
